review: 1:1 תִּרְפֶּא — the Arabic نَفْسِي تَطِيب is 'my soul is healed/is well'; the niphal-like form of רפא keeps the passive sense without adding a pronoun.

1:3 בַּיּוֹם תְּנַחֵם, בַּלַּיְלָה שׁוֹמֵר — the Arabic pairs 'by day You comfort' with 'by night a Watcher'; Hebrew keeps the two time-phrases at the head of their clauses, which is the psalm pattern (Ps 121:6).
2:1 הִרְבַּצְתָּ הַצֹּאן — 'You made the flock lie down' (Song 1:7, אֵיכָה תִרְבָּץ); the Arabic أَرْبَضْتَ الْغَنَم is that verb, and the question 'in what pastures' is Song 1:7 too.

2:3–2:4 בְּעֵמֶק מַכְאוֹב / כְּאוֹבֵד בַּמִּדְבָּר — the Arabic وَادِي الْأَلَم ('valley of pain') echoes Ps 23:4's valley; Hebrew keeps the valley and adds the lost-in-the-wilderness image of the next line.
3:3 נְהַלְנִי וּשְׁמֹרְנִי — two imperatives with the cohortative ending, the psalm voice of Ps 23:2–3 and 121:7–8.
